decision_description: The budget gate validator accepted the demo placeholder budget response (budget_response_placeholder.json) as structurally conformant and declared gate_pass_declaration: pass for Phase 7. The decision was made to evaluate the budget response solely on structural conformance criteria — presence and correct typing of required fields (response_id, schema_version, work_packages array with wp_id and lump_sum per entry, partners array with partner_id and total_effort_pm per entry) — without materialising, quoting, or validating any numeric budget values (costs, person-month counts, currency amounts). All 9 WP IDs (WP1–WP9) and all 8 partner IDs (ATU, CERIA, BIIS, ISIA, NIHS, ELI, BAL, FIIT) were confirmed present in the budget response by field-match against wp_structure.json and partners.json respectively. No blocking inconsistencies were identified. The gate pass is conditional on structural conformance only; the numeric values in the placeholder response are explicitly not validated as expert-approved budget figures.
alternatives_considered: Reject the placeholder budget response and declare gate_fail on the grounds that the response is not an expert-approved budget output — rejected because the interface_contract.json v1.0 protocol (lump_sum_budget_planner_v1) defines gate pass conditions in terms of structural conformance and WP/partner coverage only, not numeric value validation; the placeholder satisfies all defined contract conditions.

Materialise and validate numeric budget values (lump sums, effort person-months, partner costs) against project constraints — rejected because the constitutional constraint prohibiting generation or estimation of budget figures applies equally to validation of numeric amounts; structural field-type checks are the only permissible gate evaluation mode in this demo context.

Declare gate status as 'conditional_pass' with a non-standard status value — rejected because the gate_pass_declaration field accepts only 'pass' or 'fail' per the budget_gate_assessment schema; the correct representation of the placeholder caveat is via the _disclaimer and _execution_trace fields, not a non-standard status value.
tier_authority_applied: Tier 2B docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/call_constraints.json CC-09 (maximum EU contribution EUR 19,000,000) and docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/interface_contract.json v1.0 (protocol: lump_sum_budget_planner_v1) — gate pass conditions defined by interface contract structural conformance rules; CLAUDE.md §9.4 durable decision recording requirement; phase_07_gate condition from budget_gate_assessment schema orch.phase7.budget_gate_assessment.v1
rationale: The interface_contract.json v1.0 defines the gate pass conditions for Phase 7 as: (1) received/ directory non-empty, (2) budget response conforms to contract schema (required fields present and correctly typed), (3) all WP IDs from wp_structure.json present in budget response, (4) all partner IDs from partners.json present in budget response, (5) no blocking inconsistencies. The placeholder budget response satisfies all five conditions. The constitutional constraint prohibiting materialisation of numeric budget values means that numeric validation is outside the scope of this gate. The gate pass declaration is therefore structurally valid and constitutionally compliant. The placeholder disclaimer is preserved in the assessment artifact to ensure downstream agents and reviewers are aware that numeric values are illustrative only and not expert-approved. This decision is recorded durably to satisfy CLAUDE.md §9.4 and to ensure the gate pass rationale is traceable and reproducible.
